GENERAL PRINCIPLES 39 This guideline recommends that medicinal product use in pregnancy and/or breastfeeding 40 receives careful consideration and is incorporated into planning throughout investigational 41 product development from nonclinical studies through post-approval use of the product. 42 Proactive planning for obtaining data related to use in pregnancy and/or breastfeeding through 43 nonclinical and clinical studies (or the rationale for not obtaining data) should be done from 44 the early stages of formulating the development strategy for the investigational product. 45 Sponsors of drug development programs and clinical trials are encouraged to consider 46 strategies to generate data that support informed decision-making on the safety, dosing, and 47 efficacy of the medicinal product’s use during pregnancy and breastfeeding. Sponsors are 48 recommended to consult with regulatory authorities as early as possible and as needed 49 throughout the investigational product development process regarding the plans for the 50 participation of pregnant and/or breastfeeding women in clinical trials. Every effort should be 51 made to reduce the burden of study procedures on pregnant and breastfeeding study participants 52 and it is essential to avoid any undue influence or coercion when pregnant or breastfeeding 53 women are included or planned to be included in clinical trials. Early engagement with 54 appropriate stakeholders, including patients, provides opportunities to address all relevant 55 aspects of these clinical trials. 56

candidates.statement: 4.2.4 Pharmacokinetics and Dosing Considerations 272 There may be a need to modify the dose or frequency of investigational product administration 273 during pregnancy. 274 The physiological changes that occur during pregnancy may affect absorption, distribution, 275 metabolism, and elimination of the product potentially leading to an altered PK/PD profile of 276 the investigational product. In addition, the extent of these physiological changes can vary over 277 the course of pregnancy, so PK/PD should be assessed during the different trimesters and 278 postpartum. Depending on the duration of treatment, PK/PD measures should be assessed from 279 the same participant wherever possible. The postpartum assessment period should be 280 sufficiently long to understand PK/PD changes until the return to pre-pregnancy state. 281 For clinical trials that include pregnant participants, it is essential to include in the protocol 282 whether pregnant participants should receive the same dose as non-pregnant participants or a 283 different dose.
